title: Custom domain and DNS concepts
learningObjectives: Explain custom domain and dns concepts and use browser or version-control tools to diagnose and publish reliable web projects.

understand.concept: A custom domain maps a human-readable name to a hosting provider through DNS records. Common records include A, AAAA, CNAME, and TXT. DNS propagation and certificate provisioning can take time, and the correct record depends on the hosting provider's instructions.
understand.whyItMatters: Incorrect DNS records can interrupt a live site or email. Follow the hosting provider's exact values and verify ownership and HTTPS after changes.
understand.analogy: A custom domain is a public address label that DNS routes to the hosting service.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual developer tools, Git behaviour, and deployment requirements depend on the browser, repository, and hosting provider.

explain.narrative: The list describes common record purposes. Actual values must come from the selected hosting and DNS providers.

practise.guidedTask: Plan a custom-domain setup using provider-supplied records. Include verification, HTTPS, redirects, and rollback notes.
practise.independentTask: Apply the workflow to a small static site. Capture the commands or browser evidence, identify risks, and document recovery steps.
hints: Inspect actual files and browser behaviour.
Do not commit secrets or personal data.
Verify provider-specific deployment values before changing DNS.
